newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS REVERSES MOMENTUM TO CHARGE BACK INTO CONTENTION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS REVERSES MOMENTUM TO CHARGE BACK INTO CONTENTION.

text.p: Tiger Woods ran a reverse on Thursday, shrugging off a miserable 40 on the front nine before turning the tables with a red-hot 30 on the back half to leap into contention in the first round of the Masters.
The 21-year-old sensation came within one stroke of the record back-nine score at Augusta National as he zoomed to within three shots of first-round leader John Huston.
Woods was out of whack at the start, missing fairways and missing greens. He suffered four bogeys on his wayward, outward half, and got angry with himself.
"I was pretty hot over the way I was playing," Woods said about how he felt during his trip from the ninth green to the 10th tee.
"Augusta's fairways are pretty big and I wasn't able to hit them. I was driving the ball bad."
Woods reached for his 2-iron at the par-4 10th tee and somewhow regained his swing.
"The tee shot on 10, I felt I was in a good (swing) position. I then just tried to carry that swing feeling all the way through the back nine and it worked."
His silky swing restored, the race against par was on.
Woods sank a 15-foot putt for birdie at the 10th, chipped in for birdie at the par-3 12th, birdied the 13th, eagled the 15th and then birdied the 17th.

At number 15, Woods exhibited the prodigious power that has turned most par-5s into child's play for the three-time U.S. Amateur champion, who won three of his first nine tournaments after turning professional.
He crushed a drive on the 500-yard hole that left him only 151 yards to the cup. Woods flew a wedge at the pin and dropped the ball four feet from the hole and converted for eagle.
"It was a tough day initially, but I got through it," said Woods, who outshot playing partner Nick Faldo, the defending champion and winner of three green jackets, by five strokes.
